blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Semi-supervised object detection has recently been extended to DETR, where oriented boxes introduce an ambiguity that does not arise for axis-aligned boxes: the map from parameters to rectangles is two-to-one, since $(c_x,c_y,w,h,θ)$ and $(c_x,c_y,h,w,θ+π/2)$ denote the same rotated rectangle. Losses and matching costs are computed from the parameters, so two boxes that coincide in space can be far apart in the metric that drives training. A correctly localized student box is then penalized by the regression loss, and the inflated matching cost leads the Gaussian mixture model (GMM) filter to discard it. We propose Oriented Semi-DETR, which removes this ambiguity wherever a pseudo box enters training. Swap-aligned Target Selection regresses towards the encoding closer to the student prediction. A Swap-invariant Reliability Cost minimizes over the two encodings inside the matching cost, so the filter decides on geometry alone. Swap-aware Pseudo-label Denoising starts denoising earlier, ramps its loss weight linearly, and weights each query by the teacher score and encoding margin. All three are parameter-free and require no additional forward pass. Across all label ratios of DOTA-v2.0, Oriented Semi-DETR outperforms DETR-based supervised and semi-supervised baselines, with the largest gains at the strict IoU threshold.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Aerial images contain objects at arbitrary orientations, so detectors in this
domain predict oriented bounding boxes (OBBs) rather than axis-aligned boxes [ 2 , 14 ] . Annotation is expensive: a
single DOTA image may contain hundreds of instances, and each one needs four
vertices instead of two corners [ 13 , 3 ] .
Semi-supervised object detection is therefore attractive in this domain,
provided that pseudo-label noise does not become entangled with the box
representation.

Teacher–student frameworks generate pseudo labels from a teacher view and train
a student on a stronger augmentation [ 10 , 15 ] , and
an exponential moving average keeps the teacher stable [ 11 , 7 , 15 ] . Detection
transformers assign one query to each object [ 1 , 23 , 21 ] . That assignment becomes
unstable once the targets are pseudo labels, so such detectors are hard to train
under semi-supervision [ 22 ] . Semi-DETR [ 22 ] addresses this with stage-wise hybrid matching,
cross-view query consistency, and a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) that separates
reliable from unreliable pseudo boxes by their Hungarian cost. Sparse Semi-DETR [ 9 ] adds sparse learnable queries. Neither was designed
for oriented boxes, and neither resolves their two equivalent encodings.

blocks.en: 2 Method
blocks.zh: 2 方法

blocks.en: 2.1 Preliminaries
blocks.zh: 2.1 初步情况

blocks.en:
We build on Semi-DETR [ 22 ] with a DINO [ 21 ] detector adapted to oriented boxes. A teacher and a student
share the architecture, the teacher is the exponential moving average of the
student, and each iteration samples one labeled and one unlabeled image. The
teacher runs on the weakly augmented view and its outputs above a score
threshold become pseudo boxes. Every pseudo box is matched to a student query by
a Hungarian assignment whose cost combines classification, regression and
rotated IoU terms. A two-component GMM is fitted to the resulting costs and
splits the pseudo boxes into a reliable and an unreliable set. Denoising (DN)
queries follow DN-DETR’s perturbation of ground-truth boxes [ 5 ] ; in the unlabeled branch they are built from teacher pseudo
boxes, following Semi-DETR [ 22 ] . Each decoder therefore
receives three query groups, separated by an attention mask: consistency, contrastive denoising, and
matching queries, as shown in Fig. 1 .

blocks.en:
A Gaussian-based loss maps a box to a two-dimensional Gaussian, and 𝐛 \mathbf{b} and σ ⁡ ( 𝐛 ) \sigma(\mathbf{b}) give the same Gaussian, so GWD [ 16 ] and KLD [ 18 ] are already invariant under σ \sigma . Substituting such a
loss changes the metric everywhere, including the labeled branch, where the
annotation convention fixes the encoding and the ambiguity never arises.
Equation ( 3 ) leaves the metric unchanged and modifies the target
alone, so both branches remain under a single loss and supervised behavior is

blocks.en:
RIDet [ 8 ] is the closest supervised counterpart. Its
representation invariance loss also minimizes over the equivalent encodings of a
box, so its target is selected during training. Two differences
separate it from Equation ( 3 ). Its target is an annotation whose
encoding a labeling convention already fixes, while ours is a teacher
output that obeys no convention and shifts as the teacher is updated. Its
minimization is also confined to the loss, so it does not reach the Hungarian
cost, the reliability filter, or the denoising queries built from pseudo boxes,
the three places where a semi-supervised pipeline encounters the ambiguity.

blocks.en: 4 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 4 结论

blocks.en:
The parameterization of an oriented box is two-to-one: 𝐛 \mathbf{b} and σ ⁡ ( 𝐛 ) \sigma(\mathbf{b}) denote the same rectangle, so a pseudo label does not determine a unique
regression target. Because the training signal is computed from the parameters,
the ambiguity acts twice. The regression loss penalizes a student box that
coincides with the pseudo box in space, and the Gaussian mixture filter removes
that box from the unlabeled loss. Oriented Semi-DETR resolves the
ambiguity at both points. It aligns every regression target with the encoding the student
already predicts, minimizes over the two encodings inside the reliability
cost, and starts pseudo-label denoising earlier under teacher-score and
encoding-margin weights. The architecture and the per-iteration
computation are unchanged. On DOTA-v2.0 our method improves performance on every
label ratio over DETR-based supervised and semi-supervised baselines, and the
gain is largest at the strict IoU threshold. The same approach applies
wherever a teacher–student target representation admits several equivalent
encodings of one oriented object.

blocks.en: H The diagnostic in full

blocks.en: H.1 Protocol

blocks.en:
We load a training checkpoint, run the teacher on 128 unlabeled images and
keep the pseudo boxes above the usual score threshold. The raw student queries
of the same forward pass are then matched to those pseudo boxes twice. The first
pass uses the fixed regression cost, the second uses Eq. (4). The
classification and rotated IoU terms are shared between the two passes, and each
pass runs its own Hungarian assignment and fits its own two-component GMM to the
matched costs of that batch, exactly as training does. A record is one matched
pseudo box, so every percentage below is taken over matched pairs. We report two checkpoints,
20k and 180k, to show the effect at the start and at the end of training.

将伪信箱保持在通常的分数阈值以上。 学生的原始询问
同样的前方通行证,然后与这些假盒子匹配两次。 第一个
通行使用固定回归成本,第二种使用Eq. (4). 那个
分类和轮换的IoU术语由两个通行证共用,每个通行证
传球执行自己的匈牙利任务 并符合自己的两部分GMM
与这批货的成本相匹配,就像培训一样。 记录是匹配的
假盒,所以下面的每一个百分比 都占据匹配的对。 我们报告两个检查站
20k和180k,在训练开始和结束时显示效果.

The warm-up length deserves a comment because it decides which Semi-DETR [ 22 ] stage the runs are in. Semi-DETR uses a one-to-many

consistency associated with that stage, is not activated. This is our controlled

the results here speak to the one-to-many stage, while the effect of the proposed
rule in the one-to-one stage remains untested.
